3. Exploring the CDM

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-03-explore.Rmd
book-03-explore.Rmd

What you will learn

Read table and column metadata, then interpret safe counts.

This chapter uses the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection from Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Find a table 

available <- ds.omop.tables(conns = conns)
knitr::kable(available$site)

Check that observation, death and visit_occurrence exist before designing a recipe. A CDM may contain an empty table or omit a table altogether.

Read the question and answer fields 

knitr::kable(ds.omop.columns("observation", conns = conns)$site)
column_name cdm_datatype db_datatype concept_role semantic_class fk_domain is_date is_extension is_untyped_identifier is_sensitive is_blocked is_quasi_identifier
observation_id integer real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
person_id integer real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
observation_concept_id integer real domain_concept concept FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
observation_date date text non_concept ordinary TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE
observation_datetime datetime text non_concept ordinary TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE
observation_type_concept_id integer real type_concept concept Type Concept FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
value_as_number float real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
value_as_string varchar(60) text non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE
value_as_concept_id Integer real attribute_concept concept FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
qualifier_concept_id integer real attribute_concept concept FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
unit_concept_id integer real attribute_concept concept Unit FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
provider_id integer real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
visit_occurrence_id integer real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
visit_detail_id integer real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
observation_source_value varchar(50) text non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE
observation_source_concept_id integer real source_concept concept FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE
unit_source_value varchar(50) text non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE
qualifier_source_value varchar(50) text non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE

observation_concept_id identifies the question. value_as_concept_id identifies a coded answer. Filtering on the question and reading the answer are two separate choices. value_as_number is for numeric values; it is not our education answer.

Count safely 

ds.omop.table.stats("observation", conns = conns)$per_site$site
#> $rows
#> [1] 1475
#> 
#> $persons
#> [1] 670

An observation row is an answer, not necessarily a distinct person. Repeated answers mean that counting rows and counting people can give different results. Respect the returned disclosure representation; do not reinterpret a band as an exact number or a refused result as an empty table.

Identify the date field 

knitr::kable(ds.omop.columns("visit_occurrence", conns = conns)$site)

visit_end_date date text non_concept ordinary TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE

visit_type_concept_id Integer real type_concept concept Type Concept FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE

admitting_source_concept_id integer real source_concept concept Visit FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE

discharge_to_source_value varchar(50) text non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE
preceding_visit_occurrence_id integer real non_concept ordinary FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE

visit_start_date records when a visit started. visit_concept_id describes its setting, such as inpatient or outpatient. visit_type_concept_id describes the provenance of the record; it is not the field for that setting filter.

Recap

Schema exploration tells you which fields exist. Safe counts describe support without returning records.

Try it

Inspect the death table and locate its coded cause field.
